title: Scene editor E4: asset library, inspector, frame budget, the look

revisions.text:
# Scene editor E4: asset library, inspector, frame budget, the look

Step 4 of 6 of the in-game scene editor. Design page (see the layout mock): https://claude.ai/artifact/GZf1vP9iD5ChT2cx2BGD6p. Read PROJECT-BRIEF.md first and follow its standing rules. Needs E1 to E3.

## Goal
The editor gets its real layout: scene tree, asset library and history on the left; inspector and frame budget on the right; a tool rail; a hint chip. You place new props by dragging them in from the library.

## Build
1. Left panel:
   - Scene: the edit's props grouped by district (`zoneAtPoint`), added ones marked green, removed ones struck through; clicking a row selects and flies the camera to it.
   - Library: every prop the game can draw (the keys of `PROPS`, placeholders and rigged props excluded unless they work with `createPropInstances`), with a readable name, a search box and a small picture. Draw each picture once with a tiny offscreen render and cache it; do not ship picture files. New converted props must appear here with no code change.
   - Assets in `assets-register.json` that are only "received" are NOT in the game build. Do not read the register from the game. Instead show one muted line at the foot of the library: "More assets are waiting for import: see the hub's Assets page."
   - History: the undo stack as rows; clicking a row jumps to that point.
2. Placing: drag a library tile into the view (or click it, then click the ground). A striped ghost follows the pointer on the ground, snapped; it turns red with the reason when `validateEdits` would refuse the spot. Drop places it through the E1 `place` transaction.
3. Right panel (inspector): the selected prop's name, prop id and triangle count; number fields for x, z and turn in degrees (typing applies through the same transactions); snap step choice (0.25, 0.5, 1 m).
4. Frame budget: live `renderer.info.render.calls` against 300 with a bar, "this edit: +N draw calls" from `drawCallCost`, a warning colour from 270 and a refusal to place a NEW model at 300 (copies of a model already on screen stay allowed).
5. Tool rail (select, move, turn, place, remove), a hint chip that names the current tool's keys, and the top bar from E3 restyled.
6. Look: dark monochrome glass panels as in the reference, Geist-like system font stack (no network fonts), the accent used only for selection and the primary button. All editor CSS lives in one `<style>` block injected by `scene-editor.js`, so `style.css` is not touched and nothing loads in normal play. Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. It must stay usable at 1280 x 720.
7. Tests: library lists exactly the drawable props; search filters; placing from the library adds to `added` with a fresh id; the ghost refuses a spot outside the playable area; inspector fields move the prop; the budget counter refuses a new model at the limit; history jump.

## Frame rate
Library pictures: one small offscreen render per prop, done lazily while the editor is open and cached; none during normal play. Report how long the first open takes with the full library. The feel of dragging and the look are not verified in software WebGL: say so.

## Rules
- No change to `map-definition.js`, `world.js`, `town.js` or `style.css`.
- No BOM. After the change run `npm run release -- --force`, then `npm test`. Stop with tests passing; report failures honestly. If a test fails only because PROJECT-INDEX.md is stale, say so and do not edit generated files.
- Do not commit.

## Done when
You can build a small scene using only the mouse: search the library, drag three different props in, nudge one with the number fields, and watch the draw-call count change.
